detail: cv2.VideoCapture() (and VideoWriter) is opened and read, but cap.release() sits on the happy path with no try/finally — if any line between open and release raises, the capture handle is never released. Run 2026-06-23T14-01-20 (FIX tier) APPLIED the video_utils.py:40 get_video_info facet. The video_utils.py:224 extract_keyframes loop and video-quality.py:953 analyze_video facets REMAIN unfixed.

title: add_review_args registers --output unguarded, conflicting with purify/other --output registrations (first-writer-wins)
detail: image-review.py:134: add_review_args() registers --output without checking whether it is already registered, creating a semantic conflict on the unified image parser. First-writer-wins means whichever submodule loads first owns the --output dest. Same architectural smell as vbvr-duplicate-dest-registrations. Fix shape: centralize --output in _shared with one canonical registration, or use conflict_handler='resolve'.

title: image.py calls _restore.add_restore_args but 'restore' is not a documented image sub-action (dead registration)
detail: image.py invokes _restore.add_restore_args to register restore flags, but 'restore' is not listed as an image sub-action in COMMAND_NAMES / the image dispatcher, so the registration is dead. title: _arg_registered() helper inspects parser._actions — a CPython-private attribute that can break across argparse versions
detail: app/commands/_shared.py: the _arg_registered() / _option_registered() dedup-helpers iterate parser._actions to detect already-registered flags. parser._actions is a private attribute (leading underscore); CPython/argparse give no stability guarantee across versions, so the dedup logic that the entire unified-parser order-coupling pattern depends on is itself built on a fragile foundation. The load-bearing wall under the whole shared-flag skip architecture. Fix shape: prefer a parse_known_args probe or track registered dests in an explicit set rather than reaching into _actions.

title: A/B variation generate() reuses args.input_image / args.audio / ab_params across iterations — shared-state mutation yields correlated variants

Fix shape: deep-copy or re-resolve per iteration; NEVER mutate args.* across variation iterations. RETIRED: superseded by the broader sys.exit/argparse families that now absorb the variation-loop facets.

detail: Unused imports accumulate monotonically as modules land without cleanup; PEP8-ordering nitpicks compound the volume. The largest dimension in full-scope scans when no recent prune ran. NOTE import-hygiene is NOT pure noise — it also catches real bug-classes (run_config.py:202 layer inversion). Run 2026-06-23T21-29-09 surfaced 23 import-hygiene findings (DOMINANT 23/60=38%, tied for largest share) — the bulk PEP8-ordering + unused-symbol noise: video_utils.py:13 numpy as np unused (functions re-import locally, medium), video-segment.py:19 unused numpy/config/extract_keyframes_from_range (medium), lora_utils.py:1 math unused (low), postprocess.py:7 math+os unused (low), manifest.py:9 field+timezone unused (low), workflow.py:14 FOUR unused top-level dataclass/datetime/timezone/GenerationResult (low), pipeline.py:6 dataclass unused + string-annotation forward refs to undefined VAE/tokenizer/text_encoder/model (low), flux2_controlnet_pipeline.py:22 warnings unused (low), flux2_t2i_pipeline.py:181 in-function PIL.Image unused (low), import-checkpoint.py:24 dead top-level gc shadowed by in-function re-import (medium), run_config.py:223 in-function resolve_lora_path unused (low), image-controlnet.py:21 subprocess unused + 34 _FLUX_SHIFT_FACTOR/_FLUX_SCALE_FACTOR unused (low), image-i2i.py:24 datetime/timezone/_option_registered unused (low), ltx_variants.py:24 os unused (low), face_detailer.py:15 math+PIL.ImageFilter unused (low), text_encoder.py:5 numpy unused (low), image-t2i.py:20 _RESOLUTION_TIERS noqa-but-not-re-exported (info), ltx_pipeline.py:46 import app.vendor_patches noqa side-effect FP (info), run.py:17 sys.path.insert at module top (low), image-expansion.py:201 string annotations reference argparse but module never imports it (low — a REAL bug class: string forward-ref to an unimported module). The 23-finding spike is the signature of a scan that has NOT recently pruned imports. The image-expansion.py:201 string-annotation-to-unimported-module facet is the only structurally-interesting one.

title: run_meta `or` falsy-coerce overrides explicit 0.0 AND misfires on empty list [] (list-typed multi-LoRA input) — doubly dangerous
detail: Run 2026-06-22T00-32-25 (image-profile.py:530, medium): run_meta's lora_scale is built via a falsy-coalesce (`val or default`) that silently overrides an explicit lora_scale=0.0 — the same `or`-overrides-zero family, but with an extra twist: the input is list-typed (multi-LoRA action=append), so the coerce can ALSO misfire on an empty list [] (falsy). Use explicit `if val is None: val = default` AND handle the empty-list case separately.

title: _run_single never lifts LTX events out of timings dict — events lost + timings polluted (single-run path diverges from A/B path)
detail: Run 2026-06-22T00-11-42 (FIX tier, HIGH): the SINGLE-run path _run_single never popped 'events' out of the returned timings dict, silently diverging from the A/B path. GENERAL LESSON: when a feature (events capture) is added to one code path (A/B), audit the sibling path (single-run) for the same lift — divergence is silent because each path is tested in isolation.

title: Long-running network operations (CivitAI import, large safetensors download) have no retry — a single transient error kills a multi-GB import
detail: Run 2026-06-22T00-11-42 (medium): the CivitAI API GET and the subsequent multi-GB safetensors download in import-checkpoint have NO retry — any transient network blip aborts an import that may have downloaded several GB. Sibling class to mlx-review:subprocess-without-timeout. Distinct because this is HTTP not subprocess, and the cost of failure is bandwidth-wasted not fd-leaked.

title: Magic-number seed default diverges from the project-wide default (42 vs 777) — silent wrong-seed at one call site
detail: Run 2026-06-22T12-34-52 (FIX tier, medium): image-faceswap.py:385 used getattr(args,'seed',42) — a magic-number default 42 that diverged from the project-wide default 777. APPLIED: changed 42 -> 777. GENERAL LESSON: magic-number defaults are a silent-divergence trap — grep for getattr(args,'seed',<int>) and any literal != 777 is a bug.

title: SeedVR2Upscaler.upscale had no MemoryError/RuntimeError handling (unlike ZImagePipeline) — heavy Metal-allocation path unguarded
detail: Run 2026-06-22T12-34-52 (FIX tier, medium): SeedVR2Upscaler.upscale wrapped its heavy Metal-allocation body with NO try/except. APPLIED: wrapped in try/except (RuntimeError, MemoryError) with mx.clear_cache() flush. GENERAL LESSON: every heavy-Metal-allocation path (encode/decode/upscale) needs the same MemoryError guard shape, not just the flagship generate() — audit all Pipeline.*.upscale / decode entry points.

title: motion_mean aliases flicker_mean — a derived metric masquerading as independent, so a 'has motion' gate never fires independently
detail: Run 2026-06-22T12-34-52 (medium): in video-t2i2v.py the motion_mean metric is computed as an ALIAS of flicker_mean (same underlying value), so any downstream gate like 'if motion_mean > threshold' is indistinguishable from the flicker gate. Fix shape: compute motion_mean from optical-flow / pixel-displacement. GENERAL LESSON: when adding a derived metric, verify it is computed from a DISTINCT signal, not aliased to a sibling metric.

title: Any fix changing error OR behavior semantics (exception TYPE, swallow-vs-propagate, OR-fallback removal) breaks pre-existing tests asserting the old behavior
detail: Run 2026-06-22T20-15-43 (FIX tier) added a THIRD facet: the seed_sequence `count = ... or 1` -> `max(1, getattr(...))` fix broke test_shared_helpers asserting the OLD coalesce behavior; restore reverted ONLY _shared.py. This generalizes the class: ANY fix that changes behavior semantics (exception TYPE, swallow-vs-propagate, OR fallback-vs-explicit) will break tests asserting the old behavior. LESSON: whenever a fix changes behavior semantics, grep the test suite for `pytest.raises(<old type>)`, `SystemExit`, and assertions on the OLD behavior at the same locus and update those tests IN THE SAME fix batch. Fix shape: ALWAYS run grep -rn 'SystemExit|pytest.raises|count.*or.*1|or.*default' app/tests/ before merging a semantics-changing fix. The sys.exit->raise conversion is NOT automatically regression-safe; it depends on whether tests assert SystemExit at that locus — verify per-site. Run 2026-06-23T21-29-09 had 0 such regressions despite applying 17 fixes (16 type-only-narrowing + 1 prompt-file-read exception-narrowing that added a guard but did NOT change an existing exception type a test asserted on) — the type-only posture held again, confirming type-narrowing-only fixes are restore-safe.

title: Streaming subprocess.Popen with `for line in proc.stdout` + proc.wait() blocks forever if the child hangs — replace with a deadline + communicate()
detail: Run 2026-06-22T13-51-05 (FIX tier, high): image-purify._run_transformer_backend streamed the child i2i run via `for line in proc.stdout` + `proc.wait()` with NO timeout — a hung child blocks the parent forever. APPLIED: replaced with a deadline-bounded communicate(). GENERAL LESSON: any `for line in proc.stdout` + `proc.wait()` streaming pattern is a latent deadlock; prefer proc.communicate(timeout=...). Sibling to mlx-review:subprocess-without-timeout but specifically the Popen-streaming deadlock facet.

title: VLM response JSON shape accessed without KeyError/IndexError guard — a malformed LM Studio response crashes caption
detail: Run 2026-06-22T22-42-41 (FIX tier, correctness-caption-1145, high) re-confirmed at a SECOND call path: _call_vlm_multi accessed the LM Studio response as data["choices"][0]["message"]["content"] with NO guard. APPLIED: wrapped the chained lookup in _call_vlm_multi with try/except (KeyError, IndexError). GENERAL LESSON: any external-service JSON response accessed by chained key/index lookups needs a guard at EVERY call path — fixing one path does NOT cover the sibling path. LM Studio (and VLM servers generally) return variable shapes on error/timeout/truncation.

title: LTX video generate_and_save() and its sibling paths (generate_flf2v, generate_ic_lora) lack MemoryError/Metal-OOM handling — heavy Metal-allocation video paths unguarded
detail: Run 2026-06-22T22-42-41 (FIX tier, high) re-confirmed the SIBLING-PATH divergence: generate() was guarded 2026-06-22T20-15-43, but generate_flf2v() and generate_ic_lora() still wrapped their self._pipeline.generate_and_save() calls with NO try/except. APPLIED: identical try/except (RuntimeError, MemoryError) with mx.clear_cache() flush to BOTH sibling paths. GENERAL LESSON: when guarding a heavy-Metal-allocation method, grep the class for ALL generate*/save*/upscale*/decode* entry points and guard each. Run 2026-06-23T14-01-20 REJECTED by-dimension the lens_pipeline/sam3_predictor missing-MemoryError-guard findings — those modules do NOT allocate heavily enough to warrant the flagship-pipeline guard; the memoryerror-guard family applies to the flagship generate/decode/upscale video paths ONLY.

title: GpuLock.__enter__ opens the lock fd but __exit__ does not run if the body raises — fd leak on exception in the guarded command
detail: GpuLock.__enter__ opens the lock fd but only closes it for 3 narrow exception types; unexpected exceptions leak the fd+process reference. The context-manager protocol guarantees __exit__ only on normal exit or exceptions RAISED WITHIN the with-block, not on failures between fd-open and block-entry. Fix shape: open the fd inside a try/finally in __enter__. Run 2026-06-23T21-29-09 (FIX tier, type-safety-gpu_monitor-401, low) APPLIED a typing facet: switched the lock fd to binary mode, annotated IO[bytes]|None, opened with 'rb' — but the fd-leak-on-exception itself REMAINS unfixed (the type annotation + binary mode only document it, do not close it on BaseException).

title: The restore mechanism reverts ONLY the file(s) whose fix caused the pytest regression, KEEPING all other safe source fixes — verified across 6 runs
detail: Run 2026-06-22T22-42-41: restore NOT triggered (0 regressions, 12 fixes) — type-only-narrowing fixes do NOT trigger restore. Run 2026-06-22T20-15-43: restore reverted ONLY _shared.py (seed_sequence) keeping 10 source files. The restore correctly distinguishes test-contract drift / behavior-semantic-change regressions from source bugs — it is file-granular. Run 2026-06-23T21-29-09 (FIX tier): restore NOT triggered (0 regressions, 17 fixes applied incl. 16 type-only-narrowing + 1 prompt-file-read exception-guard, pytest 986/0). SIXTH consecutive clean FIX run. Confirms the type-only-narrowing + None-sentinel-discipline posture is now the stable, restore-safe norm.

title: SeedVR2 single-step Euler math hardcodes t=1000/s=0 — adversarial REJECT: multi-step schedules would need re-derivation, not a latent bug for the current single-step path
detail: Run 2026-06-22T20-15-43 adversarial REJECTED correctness-seedvr2-pipeline-277: the finding claimed SeedVR2's single-step Euler math (hardcoded t=1000/s=0) would 'silently produce wrong output' for multi-step schedules. REJECTED because the current code path is single-step by design. RETIRED: single-run record, narrow locus, not re-flagged in 4 subsequent runs — compacted. The suppress-rule still holds: ignore hardcoded single-step sampler constants unless the code actually claims/uses multi-step.

title: Promoting the multi-LoRA list->scalar peel into a typed shared helper first_or(values, default) in _shared.py — canonical reusable fix for the list-vs-scalar family
detail: Run 2026-06-22T22-42-41 (FIX tier): the recurring multi-LoRA list->scalar peel was ad-hoc at each call site. Promoted it into a TYPED shared helper `first_or(values, default)` in app/commands/_shared.py. LESSON: when the same defensive peel recurs across 4+ call sites, centralize it into one typed helper rather than re-deriving the isinstance guard each time. Run 2026-06-23T14-01-20 APPLIED the TypeVar T typing to first_or() so the peel helper preserves the element type for callers instead of returning Any.

title: RunConfig.from_json now runs a post-construction type-coercion pass — closes the argparse-default-None vs typed-dataclass gap without changing behavior
detail: Run 2026-06-22T22-42-41 (FIX tier): RunConfig.from_json loaded raw JSON values into typed dataclass fields with NO validation/coercion, and RunConfig.cfg_scale is annotated float (non-Optional) while the argparse default is None. APPLIED: added _coerce_typed_fields() — a post-construction pass that introspects the dataclass field annotations, normalizes string/numeric values, skips non-numeric and bool fields, preserves None on Optional, raises ValueError on null-in-non-Optional. LESSON: the dataclass-from-JSON boundary is the canonical place for a coercion pass — it closes the type gap WITHOUT changing behavior semantics (so no test-contract regression). Prefer type-narrowing-only fixes over behavior-semantic changes to stay restore-safe.

title: A variable assigned inside an if-branch is referenced in the else-branch (or after the if without a prior-branch default) — NameError at runtime, masked when the defining branch is the common path
detail: Run 2026-06-23T11-52-18 (FIX tier, argparse-integrity-image-profile.py-830, HIGH): image-profile.py referenced `resolved_lora` in the else (zimage) branch but it was only defined inside the use_flux2 branch. The NameError is masked in normal runs that take the defining branch; it detonates only on the alternate path. APPLIED: hoisted the `resolved_lora` assignment above the if/else so BOTH branches share the binding. GENERAL LESSON: when a variable is used in multiple branches of an if/else, define it in a scope visible to ALL consumers. The bug-class is invisible to tests that only exercise the defining branch; audit both branches when a variable is branch-local.

title: Distilled model generate() unconditionally overwrites explicit cfg_scale/stg_scale to fixed values — silent feature-disable for distilled variants
detail: Run 2026-06-23T14-01-20 (correctness-ltx_pipeline-329, medium): app/ltx_pipeline.py:329 — the distilled generate() path unconditionally sets cfg_scale=1.0 / stg_scale=0.0, overwriting ANY explicit user value passed via --cfg-scale/--stg-scale. Sibling to mlx-review:cfg-scale-literal-compare-sentinel, but distinct: this is an UNCONDITIONAL assignment that ignores the user's explicit value entirely. The distilled path legitimately needs cfg=1.0/stg=0.0 (CFG is inert for distilled models per MEMORY flux2-klein-cfg-inert-when-distilled), but the unconditional overwrite means a user CANNOT override even when they know their distilled variant benefits from a non-default value. Fix shape: only overwrite when the user did NOT explicitly pass the flag (use the default=None sentinel check), not unconditionally. Unfixed this run. NOTE: this is the video-pipeline sibling of the FLF2V auto-override family — both are distilled-model CFG overrides, both need the sentinel-discriminated fix.

title: _coerce_typed_fields silently int(True)=1 for a field annotated 'int' when run.json carries a JSON bool — type coercion treats bool as int
detail: Run 2026-06-23T21-29-09 (correctness-run_config-468, medium): app/run_config.py:468 _coerce_typed_fields coerces a field annotated 'int' via int(value), but Python int(True)==1 / int(False)==0, so a run.json that carries a JSON boolean for an int-typed field is silently coerced to 0/1 with no error signal. This is the inverse of the common 'bool is a subclass of int' trap — here the coercion pass explicitly SKIPS bool fields per the from-json lever (lever:runconfig-from-json-typed-coercion), but only when it RECOGNIZES the field as bool; a field annotated plain 'int' (not Optional[bool]/bool) that receives a JSON bool bypasses the skip and is silently integerized. GENERAL LESSON: any int() coercion of untrusted JSON values must guard `if isinstance(value, bool): raise ValueError(...)` FIRST — bool is a subclass of int in Python, so int(True) is a silent success, not a TypeError. Fix shape: add an explicit isinstance(value, bool) reject before int() coercion in _coerce_typed_fields.

title: Manifest records the input frame count, not the temporal-upscaled output count — downstream consumers miscount after temporal upscaling
detail: video-generate.py (manifest-write locus near the temporal-upscale path): the generation manifest records the INPUT frame count (pre-upscale) rather than the temporal-upscaled OUTPUT frame count. After temporal upscaling multiplies the frame count, the manifest undercounts the actual delivered frames — downstream replay/metrics/compare consumers that read frame_count from the manifest get the wrong number. Distinct from mlx-review:relay-frames-overcounting (relay inter-segment overlap) and mlx-review:adjust-frames-single-frame (min-clamp visibility): this is the temporal-upscale input-vs-output divergence. Fix shape: write the post-upscale frame count to the manifest, or record both input and output frame counts explicitly. Sibling family to the manifest-frame-count-accuracy class.

title: Stale comment claims --self-test is registered via add_common_generation_args() but video.py/video-quality.py never call it — comment diverges from the actual registration site
detail: video.py:129 and video-quality.py:112 carry inline comments asserting --self-test is 'registered via add_common_generation_args()', but neither video subcommand module actually calls add_common_generation_args() for --self-test — the flag is registered elsewhere (or per-subcommand). Pure documentation/comment drift (no runtime bug), the same docs-drift class as correctness:help-text-default-mismatch but for a REGISTRATION-SITE comment rather than a default value. GENERAL LESSON: when a shared helper's registration surface changes, grep for comments naming the helper across all command modules — stale 'registered via <helper>' comments accumulate at the boundary between shared and per-subcommand registration. Two sibling facets surfaced in one run (video.py + video-quality.py) confirms this is a multi-site drift, not a one-off.
